evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=plan phase=17. audit.codex.gpt56 and audit.claude.glm53 each publish finding ID P17-AUD-001 for the same behavior. May the plan keep only one disposition?
evals.expected_output: No. The current index contributes two distinct (audit_run_id, id) source keys. Both owning findings digests require dispositions, although one closure batch and evidence pair may close both.
expectations: Validates audit.index.json and every indexed member first.
Requires exact strict-union coverage for both run identities despite the duplicate textual ID.
Allows shared repair evidence only while preserving two source-bound dispositions.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 plan_sha256=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. The result narrative mentions an extra source edit, but no planned or incidental disposition owns that path. Can the result be sealed?
evals.expected_output: Refuse result validation because every reported changed path must be attributed to a planned or accepted incidental record.
expectations: Rejects the narrative-only unplanned correction.
Requires exact Changed paths union across result dispositions.
Does not silently add the path to the approved plan.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. A workspace test now fails because a private helper in the same batch collides with the approved implementation; fixing that helper changes no public or durable contract. What evidence and record are required?
evals.expected_output: Permit a bounded incidental repair only after causal-scope proof and focused red, then record all guardrails, changed path, and observed red/green in an I<N> result disposition.
expectations: Requires the defect to block the current green-after and remain within the causal batch surface.
Requires all protected-contract guardrails to be false and records a focused FAIL/PASS.
Creates a separate incidental-repair result record rather than mutating the approved plan.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. Verification reveals the fix also needs a new public constructor and a Cargo dependency. May this be handled as an incidental repair?
evals.expected_output: No. Public API and dependency changes breach the incidental guardrails, so apply stops and returns to a new plan/authority decision.
expectations: Rejects bounded incidental repair because public API and dependency graph would change.
Stops the current apply instead of broadening scope.
Requires a new plan and any needed authority decision.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. All checks pass and the fixed result validates, but the fixes and assurance directory are still uncommitted. Should a new $opi-audit start now?
evals.expected_output: No. Stop at materialization; the fixes and current live set must be committed and clean before a separate fresh audit or reviewer re-run is requested.
expectations: Does not invoke or authorize a new audit while the live set is uncommitted.
Requires fixes and assurance artifacts to be committed and clean.
Keeps Phase conformance authority with the later independent audit.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved plan_sha256. One indexed member byte and audit.index.json digest changed after approval, while the prose plan is unchanged. May production edits begin?
evals.expected_output: No. Apply fails admission because the plan's Audit index SHA-256 no longer matches; any membership, member, sidecar, or index-byte change invalidates approval.
expectations: Revalidates the complete live index before editing.
Rejects the stale Audit index SHA-256 even when plan_sha256 still matches the plan files.
Makes no production change and returns to a plan bound to the current live set.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved plan_sha256. The user committed only this Phase's fixed plan pair, so HEAD advanced from Remediation head, but all approved plan and live-index bytes are unchanged. Must the plan be resealed again?
evals.expected_output: No. Treat Remediation head as the committed source baseline and run the apply admission validator. Plan-only commits are admitted without resealing; preserve the exact approved digest and still check carried-in path ownership before edits.
expectations: Uses validate_assurance_artifact.py apply with --plan-sha256 from the explicit invocation.
Checks committed ancestry and permits only the current Phase's fixed plan pair in intervening commits.
Keeps the approved plan bytes and source baseline unchanged rather than requesting a HEAD-reseal loop.
Does not treat commit authorization as permission to apply a different digest.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. After the source baseline, one commit changed source and another restored it; the final source tree equals the baseline. Does the plan-only commit exception permit apply?
evals.expected_output: No. Check every intervening commit, including merge-parent diffs, rather than final tree equality. Source history outside the fixed plan pair requires a new plan even when later restored.
expectations: Rejects changed-then-restored source after Remediation head.
Rejects changes to another Phase's plan, result files, or audit artifacts under the same exception.
Preserves evidence and stops before production edits instead of rewriting the approved plan.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=plan phase=19. A validated indexed appendix points to a prior Closed finding and a retained raw test log. The current independent finding reports a failing sibling path. May the old finding join the source union or close the current one?
evals.expected_output: No. Preserve the strict union of current sidecar keys and use the appendix only to guide current verification. Recheck the exact named raw proof at remediation_head and distinguish the repaired branch from the current failure; historical Closed and old IDs have no disposition authority.
expectations: Validates the current set before reading its advisory appendix.
Does not add old source keys, merge findings by historical similarity or add lineage/prior_occurrences/prior_disposition fields.
Bases confirmation, severity, closure and clustering on independently verified current evidence.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=plan phase=19. The appendix names a raw exact-client matrix log whose SHA-256 matches and whose test passed. The selected client bytes have changed since that run. Is the current finding refuted?
evals.expected_output: Not from that log alone. Recheck command results and executed count, source/build/client/material identities and the proved predicate at remediation_head. Prove relevant dependencies unchanged or rerun invalidated checks within existing authorization; otherwise retain the applicability limitation.
expectations: Distinguishes raw-byte authenticity from current behavioral applicability.
Does not inherit a historical success or start paid/provider calls without their existing authorization.
Keeps unavailable or inapplicable proof unconfirmed rather than Refuted.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=plan phase=17. The valid current indexed report is a legacy report without a historical appendix. Should remediation browse history/ or refuse the report?
evals.expected_output: Neither. The report remains fully consumable. Verify every current source key normally and do not search history or prior remediation artifacts to reconstruct missing advisory rows.
expectations: Accepts valid legacy report groups without requiring retrofit.
Does not turn the bounded appendix exception into general historical browsing.
Preserves complete current finding coverage.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=19 with the approved digest. After approval, append-history added an advisory section while preserving all core bytes and findings. The index now binds the new report hash. May apply proceed because the findings are unchanged?
evals.expected_output: No. The full report and exact live index are approval inputs. The appendix invalidates the old Audit index SHA-256 binding even with unchanged findings, so stop before production edits and return to a plan bound to the current set.
expectations: Rejects stale approval rather than exempting advisory-only changes.
Does not rewrite the approved plan retroactively.
Retains the unchanged independent finding authority while requiring a new plan binding.
